utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that both parties would like to raise a preliminary matter. Mr. Lukic, you go first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Me first? Thank you, good morning, Your Honours. My intention is actually to help everybody to fill in the next week's time since we are missing one witness, so I was thinking of asking Your Honours to allow me 50 per cent increase in my time estimate with this witness, and I announced it to the Prosecution. I didn't see that they have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's confirmed by nodding. We'll consider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One hour and 45 minutes is 50 per cent of 3 and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider it. Ms. Hochhauser?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I just briefly wanted to put two procedural things on the record but it can be done as the witness is brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be brought in and meanwhile we will listen to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: First, I wanted to inform the Chamber that the B/C/S version of the supplemental information report from P01904 has now been uploaded into e-court under that evidence number. That was the one that was missing the B/C/S translation of the last page. Additionally I was informed, and it seems upon review of the record, that yesterday at 65 ter 09945, which was repeated a number of times in relation to this -- the 360-degree photos that went in, there are times when the record records it as 00945. So I wanted to just clarify that the 65 ter number and it was repeated again and again with often a letter from the alphabet after it is actually 09945.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at my notes, I may have made that mistake several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Ms. Hochhauser will now continue her examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn please to Scheduled Incident F12 which is the 18 November 1994 shooting death of Nermin Divovic and his mother Mrs. Sokolovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if we could play please the first few second the of P671 MFI, it's a video that's already obviously been MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: We can stop it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, the portion of this video was played in court with another witness. Do you recognise this P671 MFI?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And we heard you say there, well actually can you just tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the filming of the incident with the victim witness, Mrs. Sokolovic and myself that was filmed in June 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And that was under the same circumstances as you've described to us for all of these videos; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And we heard you say specifically 15 June of 2006 was when -- was when this film was made although the incident occurred November; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honours, I would tender P671 MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, could you refresh my recollection as to why it was MFI'd at the time? Was it that you wanted to introduce it later through another witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it was used with expert Patrick van der Weijden who didn't have the personal knowledge to introduce it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that there are no objections. Madam Registrar? The number is there already therefore P671 is now admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, having stood in that location and also -- sorry withdrawn. Have you ever been in the Metalka building or up towards the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have been inside and in front of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is that the alleged origin of fire for this incident?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can you tell us is there a clear line -- is there a clear line of sight between the Metalka building and the location on this street where we can see you standing with Mrs. Sokolovic?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there is, especially when the leaves are off the trees.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could turn for a moment to Exhibit P3, e-court page 25, and if anybody has the hard copy it's page 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, if we can start with looking at the picture -- sorry -- on the left of the screen, can you tell us the intersection that we see there, is that the same intersection that's -- that we see in the -- in the video that's now in evidence as P671?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And the zebra crossing that's visible, the white striped lines, that are visible at that intersection, can you tell us, having stood there, if you've stood there, can you tell us about the line of sight from the Metalka building to that zebra crossing?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The line of sight is unobstructed. It's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you just for clarity tell us -- describe to us where on this photo the Metalka building is?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the -- if you go straight -- this -- this photo is taken from the north looking south, so if you proceed straight south along the road which leads -- almost bisects the photograph, the Metalka building is the red and white brick building at the end of that street just across the river. So the Metalka building would be mid-point of the photograph at the top.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us looking at the photograph on the right just to give us the vantage point explain to us there what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The photograph on the right was taken from the south looking north, the Metalka building is in the bottom left corner, immediately beside the river, and the same street leads directly north to the Holiday Inn which is the yellow and brown building mid-point to horizontally towards the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am a bit confused about where you said the red and white building. You said if you proceed straight along the road, which leads almost -- and bisects the Metalka building, is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a little unclear, Your Honour. If I could try to explain again. The Metalka building is at the top of the photograph. It's halfway across horizontally. It's red brick with white almost stripes running down it, and it's a bit of a curved building. The street -- I'm sorry, the street that contains the zebra crossing leads directly in that -- sorry, in that direction but it stops at the river, just before the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just see -- I see three large buildings, all three slightly bent, and it's the one, if I understand you well, bending towards us on the left photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at the other photograph, it is the building, if you draw a line from a more or less reddish building which I could imagine is the Holiday Inn, and then just straight down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: For clarity of the record that we just made, could you with the assistance of the Court Usher just circle the Metalka building in both pictures and draw with a line the line of the -- draw with a line, the line of the street that you're saying has the clear line of sight to where Mrs. Sokolovic is standing with you in that video?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What confused us is that the -- it's difficult to see that it's red or white. It looks more whitish than anything else. It's clear now. I take it that you want to tender this marked double photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number P2401, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2401 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we can turn to F13 which is the 23 November shooting of a tram with passengers, and I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart please to show us what is now P2396 which is the 360-degree photo for this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, actually, right there, can you tell us what we see on the screen now? We see tram tracks and then a zebra crossing, can you tell us what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is the same location that we just looked at, the same street that we just looked at in the two photographs. The zebra crossing is the zebra crossing that we were speaking about in the previous incident, and proceeding straight up the street to the left on the left-hand side of the photograph, is a direct line to the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And if we could go to the right, please, and see this video?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I see we are just passing that yellow building is the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's the Holiday Inn, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to stop just a little bit further, sorry, if we can go a little further. Yes, right here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Mr. Hogan, we see sort of a curve in the tram tracks there, sometimes called an S-curve. And can you tell us whether the location of that curve has moved at all from the time of the confrontation period to the time of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. That -- the S-curve has always been there since the outbreak of the war, even before.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Is that true of both of them? We see there is an island and the track curves on both sides of that island. Is that true for both sides?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could please see associated exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we finish the 360-degrees?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Of course, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we now perhaps stop here because that's where we started. Where now is the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Metalka building is directly ahead. I think if you zoom in you'll be able to see part of the building through the leaves of the trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now it becomes more visible. At the end of the street, we see just a little piece of a whitish building just above where we see the cars, is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's exactly right, Your Honour, that is the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn, please, to incident F16, which is the 6 March 1995 wounding of Tarik Zunic as he walked home from school. Could we please see the associated exhibit with the reserved number P2387, which was 65 ter 23187, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, this is a photograph that you marked in the Karadzic case and it's in the prior testimony, to indicate Sharpstone. Can you tell us where this photo was taken from?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This photo was taken from the spot the witness indicated he had been standing when he was shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is it the red -- the red circle that's marked indicates the location of Sharpstone?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct. You can see the rocks and the trees on the ridge within that red circle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And that's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask, has the distance been measured between sharp rock and this position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it has been measured by the sniping expert but I cannot recall what those figures are at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 29 in e-court of again Exhibit P3, and it's page 25 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: There is a caption on the bottom of this page that reads, "View from Spicasta Stijena, Sharpstone." Can you comment on the accuracy of that caption? Do you know what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I see it in e-court, and I recognise this view from Sharpstone, looking towards the south-east.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And are you able to see on this photograph where Tarik Zunic was walking when shot?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe -- yes, I can see the location.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Are you able to mark it?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Please do that.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And you've just marked with a circle around a house. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct. He was standing in front of that house on the street, where -- when he indicated the spot where he had been wounded, and from that location, in front of that house, is where we did that filming and took that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could tender this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 29 on document P3 as marked by the witness receives number P2402, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we remove the picture, could the witness please indicate Sharpstone on that picture, if it is visible at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Sharpstone is actually from where the picture was taken, so the camera is on Sharpstone looking at the location where the young boy was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I think also to illustrate Your Honour's question though if we could turn to the next page in this exhibit of P3, which is page 30. Sorry, page 30 in e-court, page 26 if you have the hard copy in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: There is also a caption on the bottom of this page, and there are several locations marked in this photograph. Can you take us through it please and comment on the accuracy of these markings?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is the reverse angle viewed from the south looking north. In the mid -- middle of the photograph towards the top vertically, the location marked Spicasta Stijena is the B/C/S words for Sharpstone and that is the location from where the photograph was taken in the previous exhibit. To the left or to the west of Sharpstone is a hill with a communications tower -- or two communications towers on it. It's called Grdonj. That's as you can see a bare feature. And F16 with an arrow is pointing to the location where the sniping incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And would the location from which this picture was taken point -- taken from, this vantage point, would that be from Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I think this might have been taken from a helicopter in June of 2006 by my colleague. He was taking a number of aerial photographs during that mission.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Would the helicopter have been in the area of Mount Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It would have been over Sedrenik. Trebevic would have been directly south of the helicopter. So the helicopter would have been probably mid-point between Trebevic and Sharpstone.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, can you explain to us -- the caption on the bottom says view to Sedrenik, Grdonj, and Spicasta Stijena from Mount Trebevic. Is that an accurate or inaccurate and if it's not accurate can you please tell us how because I'm slightly confused by your prior answer.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It -- you can see this view from Trebevic but you would need very good binoculars or telescope to get this kind of detail. Trebevic is a little bit too far away to be this -- have this close-up view.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And when it says "View to Sedrenik," and I'm sorry for my pronunciation, can you tell us where that is in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I missed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Does that appear in the photograph, view to S-e-d-r-e-n-i-k?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Sedrenik is the settlement area here with the houses of Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 19710 on the monitor, which is a collection of BiH reports relating to site visits at various locations in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, have you had the opportunity to look through -- gesundheit, have you had the opportunity to look through the collection of reports here?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And see, for example, on the first page of this report, it says "regarding the on-site investigation carried out at number 6A, Grabovica Street, 13th floor of the skyscraper apartment number 51." Do each of the reports name a different location -- name a different location?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: All right. And are you familiar with the locations named in this document?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you tell us in -- in looking at these documents, are they reports about snipers' nests, about the finding of snipers' nests?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, are you aware of on-site investigations conducted by the BiH into sniping locations as described in 19710?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Were you asked to assist in putting together a map indicating on that map the locations named in this series of reports as snipers' nests?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could for a moment see 65 ter 30307 on the screen, please, this is a document that was e-mailed, Your Honours, to the Chamber, I believe, or referenced in the e-mail to the Chamber and to the Defence. It was created last week, disclosed on the day that it was created and we sought to add it to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what it is, please, that we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is a street map of a portion of Sarajevo with red boxes or rectangles enclosing the buildings which correspond to the street addresses that are mentioned in those documents that we just had a look at, the investigation documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And does this map accurately reflect those locations along with the specific apartment numbers of where 1970 -- 19710 records snipers' nests being found?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would tender at this time 65 ter 30307 and 19710.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would object, at least for now, and after our cross-examination, we have to put some more questions on these documents, what is involvement of this witness in creation of these documents. So, what's his knowledge about the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are two issues. The first is to have it added to the 65 ter list, I take it. Any objections to that? Perhaps already for you to know, Mr. Lukic, that we will grant your request to have it MFI'd first and only to decide on admission once you have cross-examined the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not object to add that document to the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Leave is granted to add 65 ter 30307 and -- no, let me -- yes, and 19710, the last -- the first one was already on the 65 ter list and the --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: 19710 was already on the 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so there is no need, and 30307 leave is granted to add it to the 65 ter list and we will decide on admission and MFI it for the moment. Ms. Hochhauser, we need a number for both isn't it, yes, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19710 receives number P2403 and document 30307 receives number P2404, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn back to P3, Exhibit P3, and if we could have page 39 in e-court, please, which is page 34 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, first, can you describe, please, for us, if you're familiar with the slope of the road from the area marked for the G13 shelling incident to the RTV building; in other words, can you describe it in words and if you know the approximate difference in elevation, can you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Hochhauser, shouldn't the witness at least tell us what at first we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we are looking at, please?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is a view of a part of Sarajevo, the large concrete building at the top of the photograph, with the satellite dishes on top and in front is the Sarajevo Television building. The main road, the large road running across the photograph directly in front of the television building is Zmaja od Bosne, the main road of Sarajevo where the tram tracks run down. The built-up area with the apartment building on the left and centre of the photograph is Alipasino Polje, and this view is from the south looking north, from a -- from an aerial view, from a helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And in terms of the various elevations, south going north, so from the bottom of the photograph to the top of the photograph, can you describe in terms of elevation, this area?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The elevation falls from the location of the camera towards the television building. In other words, these red -- these single family houses in the foreground, with the red roofs, are higher in elevation than the buildings in the top of the photograph. The building circled and marked G13 is, in my estimation, approximately 30 to 35 metres higher in elevation than the street, the main street, in front of the television building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And are we looking from south to north here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Have you measured, using a scaled map, to judge the distance from th area of G13 where the alleged -- excuse me, where the incident G13 was pointed out to you to have occurred, to the RTV building?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have, and the distance that I measured was approximately 650 to 700 metres. It was a -- I couldn't get more precise than that. It was a rough scale.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could go backwards in this exhibit, please, to page 34 of P3, this aerial map book.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And sir, just to alert you to what I'm going to do now, I'm going to take you through a number of the pages in this book related to shelling incidents and just ask you about the photographs. So we are looking at page 34 of P3. Can you please orient the Chamber to what it is we are looking at and comment on the caption?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is the site of the -- what's known as the soccer game shelling in June of 1993. There were two shells that landed that day. The camera is situated on the spot where the witness indicated the first shell had landed. In the first photograph is a memorial to the victims and that's actually the same location where one of the goal nets had been located during the soccer game. And then the next two photographs pan towards the north-west direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And I think you told us before that with these 360-degree images where in the shelling incidents where there were multiple impacts you chose the one that was -- you were guided to by the witness or victim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's correct. We actually did 360-degree photographs from both shelling locations -- shelling impact locations that the witness indicated to us. But this one obviously is the first shell. These images. MS; HOCHHAUSER: Turn to the next page of the -- of P3, please, which is page 35 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And this bears the marking of G7, 4 February 1994 charged incident. Can you again, please, orient us on this photograph and tell us whether the places as they are marked, so the markings on the photograph, are accurate?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. They are accurate. This is an aerial photograph, again from a helicopter, taken by my colleague. The view is over Dobrinja and we are looking to the south-west -- no, I'm sorry, it's directly south. And the -- there were three shells that landed on that date and they're all-- the impact points are all within that yellow circle that we see marked G7.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could turn please to page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are looking south here? I see, at the back, I see the airport with a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: There are --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we turn to page 37 for a moment in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: We can see here the locations marked for G15, G6 and G13 which you told us earlier in your testimony yesterday are accurate based on your -- based on the measure -- based on the locations pointed out to you and the GPS recordings that you took. I dealt already with G13, sort of out of order so I'm going to take you now to the next page which is page 38 and ask you to comment on this page, which is relevant to the G6 charged incident. And that, sorry, is the 22, 1994, three mortar shells.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is the -- these are images from the 360-degree photograph that were taken from one of the shell impact locations. And I believe the photograph on the bottom, the larger photograph, was taken from the second impact site. The first three, along the top, were from the first impact site, which correspond to the marking G6 on e-court page 37. And the larger photograph, on the bottom, corresponds to the second impact site, which is at the south end of that building marked G6.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could turn, please, to page 40 of the map book in e-court which is page 35 in the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And again same question. I'll just ask you to orient us to this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This is a view, an aerial view, of Alipasino Polje, and taken from a helicopter, looking to the north-west. And the large -- the busy road that we see bisecting the photograph from the top left to the bottom right is the same road that ran past the TV building in one of the previous photos that we looked at, and this location is approximately five to -- 500 to 800 metres further west from -- from that TV building site. The red circle that we see marked G15 is the location where a modified air-bomb landed and exploded on the -- actually on the footpath just behind the bushes that we see divided by the red circle.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And finally, if we can see, please -- finally for the map book, if we can see, please, in succession pages 42 and 43 in e-court which are pages 37 and 38 in the hard copy, and again I'll just ask you whether the captions on that page are accurately marked to the best of your -- the markings on the page are accurately marked to the best of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The markings I see are G18, Markale 2 and G8 Markale 1 and arrows pointing to correspondent -- corresponding locations and in my opinion, those are properly marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to a different topic. In your prior testimony, which is now in evidence as P2379, you discuss beginning at e-court page 20, an assignment that you received with respect to a video by Colonel Demurenko and it's a video which has also been referenced at this trial by the Defence, for example at transcript page 7563.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could have associated exhibit, which is now -- now has the MFI number, I believe, P2380 on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you please explain this graphic in terms of the photograph that you took in your assignment as to how would one use this graphic in looking at those photographs on their own, for example, once it's in evidence?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The photograph is a view, an aerial satellite view, of a portion of the city of Sarajevo and the area to the south. The two white lines meet at the top at the Markale 2 market, Markale 2 incident site, which is the closed market. The line on the left runs at 176 degrees from that market and the line on the right runs at 170 degrees from the market. You'll see on the left line, the 176 degree mark -- line, various distances indicated by white arrows, white arrow heads, and there you'll also see in black printing, WP, and then a number, WP 1, WP 2, WP 3, up to WP 10. The WP stands for way-point, which is what a GPS unit gives as a term for a marked location. So when I attended various locations marked by WP, and saved that location into the GPS unit for a reading, I marked it as a way-point, WP, the first 1, WP, the 10th one, and I should add that this area to the south of the city is Mount Trebevic. The mountain rises further to the south. This is from the south looking north. But from the area of the city, where the lines meet, up until the bottom of the photograph, the land is continually rising.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And why was it that the angles 170 and 176, that those degrees were chosen?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the video that Colonel Demurenko produced and had broadcast in I believe it was at the end of August or early September 1995, speaking about the Markale 2 shelling incident, he demonstrated a line of 176 degrees. He drew a chart and he indicated various distances along that line of 176 degrees. The purpose of that demonstration on his video was that, as he explained, having referred to a mortar firing table for a 120-millimetre mortar, he worked out the only possible six distances from which a mortar could have been fired to impact the Markale 2 shelling site. He then explained on the video that he attended the three sites which were located on the VRS side of the confrontation line and then he further explained on the video that, having examined those three sites within a ten-metre radius, he determined that those -- the ground was not suitable for supporting a mortar and that he saw no signs of a mortar having been fired from those locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. With the Chamber's permission, what I'd like to do is to provide investigator Hogan this exhibit that we now see on the screen along with the index, that is the first page of MFI P2382, which is the index for the photographs so that he can use them for reference as he takes us through the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed as suggested.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we could see P2382, please, on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness, apparently he has looked at the video of Mr. Demurenko. When he had chosen on the table the firing positions, had he calculated the difference in elevation between where the shell landed and where these firing positions were, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on his video, he did not mention those calculations. On his video, he showed the UNPROFOR reports and the local police reports of the on-site investigation which determined the angle of impact of the mortar shell on the pavement and the angle of approach of the mortar shell from the south to the Markale market site. But I saw no indication of difference in heights in calculating the distances to the possible mortar launch sites.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, is this the first page of the exhibit? Excuse me one second.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm afraid there is actually an index, that goes -- should be the first page of this exhibit, which we haven't uploaded and which investigator Hogan now has. I would ask permission to go through the photographs and then upload the index.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If we need them while listening to the testimony, then it could be put on the ELMO but temporarily awaiting the uploading.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And just to describe, does the -- does the index contain ERN numbers related to each photograph and the location or way-point from which you took that series of photographs?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. With the exception of the first seven or eight photographs which I had just taken from a high point on the mountain because it was not within the range of the various -- the 176 or 170 degrees. The first ones I just took for orientation of all parties of where this mountain was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And I believe you took over 100 -- over a hundred photographs but we've selected a small selection of those to tender now. Can you please, as we go -- can you please take us through them and explain what we are looking at, orient the Chamber to the small selection of photographs we have taken and tell us your observations in relation to your assigned task related to Colonel Demurenko's video for each photograph, your observation?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This first photograph was taken from the upper slopes, not -- approximately three-quarters of the way to the top of Mount Trebevic and it's a view looking north towards the eastern part of the city. You can actually see the view from here of Sharpstone, Grdonj and Sedrenik which we had been discussing earlier today. The part of the city to the left of the photograph is the beginning of Bascarsija, the old part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And is this one of the photographs that's listed from a particular way-point or is it one of the ones that you described earlier to us was taken for -- to orient ourselves?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is one of the ones that were taken from the upper slopes just to orient ourselves where this -- the mountain was located in relation to the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's just been pointed out to me that it may be time for a break. I realise I've gone over my estimation I would ask for permission after the break to just continue through this last exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This would be the last one?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it would take how much time?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I think we have approximately seven or eight photographs to go through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the Defence, whether they would prefer to have the whole of the examination-in-chief concluded before the break in seven, eight minutes? Would that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whatever Your Honour rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it doesn't make any difference to you I would say let's take the break now. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the opportunity to decide on admission of P2380 up to and including P2388. These are exhibits related to Mr. Hogan's testimony. The Registry has filed an internal memorandum wherein the provisionally assigned exhibit numbers are linked to the 65 ter numbers, and P2380 up to and including P2388 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser please proceed for the last seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan I'm just going to ask you as we go through -- as you take us through these photos if you can reference on the record the ERN number that appears on the top of each photograph since I think that the e-court page pagination will be different once we get the index properly uploaded and if you can continue taking us through to orient us where we are, tell us the way-point if there is one from which the photograph was taken and your observation regarding the given assignment.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Certainly. The -- the first photo that we are looking at now has ERN 06197138 and, as I say, that's looking north from about three-quarters of the way up Mount Trebevic, and in the middle of the photograph we can see the area of Sedrenik, Sharpstone and Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'll ask you to -- if you don't mind and if it's all right you can just indicate when you're ready for the next photograph and we can move on. So I think you're ready for the next one?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Any time. And this photograph is ERN 06197139. Again, that's from the upper slopes, about three-quarters of the way up Mount Trebevic looking a little bit northwest, and you can see a large part of the city, including the -- on the big stadium, the Kosevo hospital, the Lion Cemetery, and a large part of the central city and we are ready for the next. And this is ERN 06197140. Again, from one of the -- from the upper slope of Mount Trebevic, looking a little bit further west from the previous photograph, and we can see mount Hum, or Hum hill, the area of Pofalici, Velesici and the extreme right, just below that large cemetery, is the area of Ciglana. And we are ready for the next one. This is ERN 06197148. This photograph was taken from way-point 2, marked on the map at -- sorry, marked on the satellite image at distance 3.600 metres from Markale market. And this is a farm stead at this location. The camera is facing south, so the city is behind the view and the viewer is looking south in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. And your observation about suitability for firing from this type of location?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In my opinion, this is a perfect location to site a mortar. It's flat, it's stable.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Next photograph.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is photograph 06197154. This is another photograph taken from way-point 2, and this is actually looking back towards the city and you can see in the middle of the photograph a white jeep-type vehicle. That was my vehicle that I arrived in, and I had taken the previous photograph from directly in front of that vehicle. So this is a reverse angle, and again, you can see prime ground for locating any kind of a weapon systems in this flat, stable meadow. And the next photograph. This is photograph 06197155, and this, again, from way-point 2, this photograph was taken by me from the location just in front of my white vehicle, and this is the view to the east. This ridge is part of Mount Trebevic and the ground rises higher to the right and straight ahead, but the additional slopes of the hill, of the mountain, are hidden behind this initial ridge. And again we can see flat, stable meadow and even on the other side of this little shed, there are locations where a weapon system could very easily be located. And the next photo. This is photo 06197160. This photograph was taken from way-point 3, and on the satellite image that is located 3.400 metres from Markale. The view is looking south and we can see the red roof of the farmstead from the previous set of photos in the middle distance, centre of the photograph. Again, a meadow, hayfield, in my opinion it's suitable for siting a weapon system in this location. And the next photo. Photograph ERN 06197162. Again, from way-point 3. This photograph was taken looking north -- yes, north-east towards the tree-line, and, again, I believe this land is suitable for siting a weapon system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I can imagine that you describe areas as flat or stable, et cetera, but whether it's suitable for a weapon system requires some kind of expert knowledge. What you need exactly. And I do not think, unless a basis is laid for that, that the witness can give such an opinion. Again, unless there is a basis laid for that. Where it's flat you can you can tell us. Whether it's a meadow, you can tell us as well, that's common knowledge but suitable for weapon systems is a different matter. Ms. Hochhauser, if you want the Chamber to consider that and to rely on that, then you should lay a basis for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well, investigator Hogan, in the video that was the -- was the reason -- the video by Colonel Demurenko that was the reason that you went out on this task, was there a reason that he said that these places were unsuitable?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I recall him saying on the video that he had seen that the locations he went to were steep and rocky.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you are saying, you didn't see anything steep or rocky there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in these locations, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay. Continue. If we can -- I don't know if we are at the end of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure. If we can see the next one. This is 06197163. This, again, was taken from way-point 3 and this is actually a close-up of the tree-line that we had just seen in the previous photograph just showing the close-up of that area. And we are finished with this one. This is 06197173. This photograph was taken from way-point 5, marked on the satellite image, a little bit to the east of the 170 degree mark at approximately 2.750 metres from Markale Market. This photograph was taken by me because it is at an intersection of a number of small roads that lead off into the forest. It appeared wide, stable and sheltered area. And it was within a 5-degree margin of error of the 170 degree mark, which was the actual determination of the angle at which the -- during the UNPROFOR report -- investigation, they determined that 170 degree was the actual angle of attack, approach of the mortar shell which impacted at Markale, plus or minus 5 degrees, of course. And as you see, it's flat, appears stable and certainly provides shelter.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The next photo, unless we are at the end.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is 06197174. Again, from way-point 3 -- I'm sorry, 7174. This is from way-point 5 again. From that same intersection. And this is the view looking -- this is the view looking back west towards the direction of the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And finally, if we can bring up the next one, which is 7178.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: 06197178 is once again way-point 5, and it is one of the photographs that I took in a circle at that the location, the previous ones that we had just seen, and this is looking towards the south. So the slopes of Trebevic would rise behind these trees and this is the edge of the clearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're looking away from the city here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, in this photograph here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, that concludes my examination. Thank you for your patience. Thank you, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we continue, one question, I have not seen on any of these photographs a direct line of sight from any of those positions down to the city itself. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the photographs that we -- the locations that we have shown here, no, there was no direct line of sight to the city, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, Mr. Lukic, before we -- I give you an opportunity to start your cross-examination, I have one question. Yesterday, the Prosecution has made a few requests and we have not asked for your position on those. You remember it was to reconsider the -- well, what the Chamber announced as it being inclined not to admit part 1. Is there anything you'd like? You have not raised any matter yesterday. Was it your intention to do so or would you say, well, that's the request, let the Chamber decide as they deem fit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm more concentrated on Mr. Hogan right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that. At the same time it's an urgent matter and that's the reason I'm raising it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we answer on Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not at all. We want --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then after the break let me consult with my colleagues. It's regarding those 900 associated exhibits --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- With one of the experts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we gave a statement about that and the Prosecution asked us to reconsider it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. After the break is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the Chamber wants to give guidance to the Prosecution, if possible, today. We hear from you after the break. Apologies, Mr. Hogan, to leave you in the midst of other matters. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic. And you had -- by the way you had a request to take more time for cross-examination. The Chamber has considered that request. We'll first see how the cross-examination will be conducted. So therefore, you'll receive further reports from the Chamber later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and I just want to emphasise that the Prosecution used double time from the time they estimated when we did our first estimation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has noted that as well. We'll see how cross-examination develops and especially whether you will stay within the limits of what this witness can tell us or whether you would go beyond that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have seen from your statements that you were a member of the RCMP in Canada.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was your official position in RCMP?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police is a federal police force but it also is contracted out to eight of the ten provinces and all the northern territories, to do the everyday policing. Members are moved and transferred from spot to spot and duty to duty throughout their service, to give what the management wants to call a well-rounded career, so I in my police service, did everything from organised crime, drug investigations, criminal intelligence, to highway patrol, to municipal policing, to northern reserve policing. It was a well-rounded career.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that you never did any forensic, on-site investigations?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did many on-site investigations and I worked with the -- what we called them ident persons, to preserve and obtain physical evidence, but I was not qualified for dusting for fingerprints or that sort of forensic investigation. I'm sorry, but could I have a little bit more volume on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, you did not testify before the Court while you were working for the RCMP in anything related to reconstruction of crimes?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by reconstruction of crimes, because with every trial and testimony given in any trial, the crime has to be reconstructed for the Court. So I'm not sure exactly what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While you were working for the RCMP, you never testified before the Court on topics related to forensic evidence found on the crime scene, the way it was found, how it was kept?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I routinely collected the evidence, preserved the evidence, the physical evidence, and submitted that evidence to the crime lab, but any tests that were conducted on that physical evidence were -- I could not testify on the results of those tests unless they were in a certificate form. Usually the scientists or the ident member would explain the process of testing, physical testing or chemical testing of that evidence. But I collected it, preserved it and submitted it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- the question was whether you ever testified before a court. Did you ever testify about what you said were your tasks, that is to collect it, preserve it and submit it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, then, that your work was not independent, that you had to work in cooperation with a forensic laboratory or a forensic technician?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the word "independent" has a lot of meanings. If it means that for the final research you are dependent on others that's one, but independent could also mean not being influenced by undue influences. Your answer was about the technical dependence or that you felt that were you nevertheless dependent on instructions given when you, for example, would testify in court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To clarify on His Honour's comments, in our police force, the attending officer is in charge of that investigation. When I attended the scene, I took charge of that investigation. An when the -- if an ident member came out to obtain fingerprints or photographs, I was still in charge. Of course, he was the expert in obtaining fingerprints but I was the one that was directing what areas I wanted tested. As far as testifying in court, of course, the -- there was no direction from the crime lab or the ident member or anybody else. I testified as the -- as the full truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I did not intend to say that you received instructions before testifying. I meant precisely what you just said. But let's move on. Did you consult a book or a manual for conducting your analysis about sniper locations in this case?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't believe so. A book or a manual? I don't recall consulting a book or a manual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please be more precise on where the witness makes analysis of a sniper location and what kind of an analysis, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today, the Prosecution offered an exhibit, we opposed that, I cannot find it right now, we said that first it had to be marked for identification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you're referring to the plotting on the map, the witness has produced, then that's exactly the reason why I asked what do you mean by an analysis of a sniper location, because I did understand from that document that the only thing the witness did is to look at the report, what location was described therein, and then to plot that on a map and not to analyse in any way a sniper position. That's the reason why I asked it. It's simply plotting on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we challenge the value of that document, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay, but don't ask this witness about that, because the only thing the witness did is to transplant what he found in the document, right or wrong, and then to put it on the map. So don't ask this witness about whether these reports were right or wrong unless you find anything in his statement expressing anything of that. What I understood was just plotting on a map, which is not the same as an analysis of a sniper position. And I don't think the witness expressed himself on that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you whether you could tell us whether you consulted some specially trained persons for examining various crime scenes, what you did in Sarajevo for the purposes of this trial, for this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The -- Mr. van der Weijden and before him a British officer named Mr. Hinchcliffe, were sniping experts who we consulted for the various Sarajevo trials because they had obvious expertise in the capabilities of firearms and the selection of firing points. So -- but they -- I did not consult them per se because my task with them was just to show them the various locations and they testified independently of any other influence that I had or input I had.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I would also just ask for a clarification of what Mr. Lukic means when he says examining various crime scenes, what he means by "examination."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand from the answer of the witness that the witness said his task was then just to show the various locations and I take it that these locations you found them on the basis of what witnesses told you or what you found in those reports when you plotted it on a map and then took the persons to that place. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. But the witness had shown us the exact location prior to me showing the sniping experts. So the witness took us to, as we saw in the videos and the 360-degree panoramas, the witness or victim took me to the location, and then in subsequent missions I took the sniping expert back to that location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever do military service in the army of any country?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity of being trained by military professionals in relation to mortar activity?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had no formal training in mortar activity, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say that you had no formal training, did you ever attend the firing of a mortar and if so, how many times and at which locations?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did, at -- the Dutch military was kind enough to give a demonstration for not only myself but a great many other Tribunal personnel. We went to their firing range in the north of Holland, maybe 12 years ago, I believe, and they fired artillery and they fired mortars, but that was, like, one morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many firings took place, and do you know which calibre of weapon was used?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I intervene again. Often I say time granted for cross-examination we will closely monitor how cross-examination developed. Today I said something different. I said we'll see how cross-examination develops and especially whether you will stay within the limits of what this witness can tell us or whether you'd go beyond that. I expressed those words because the Chamber had some concern that you would go far beyond what the witness claims he can tell us, and it's now for the fourth time that I get the feeling that you go there. Would you please keep that in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We heard the witness testify today about how convenient locations were for mortars, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I stopped him there. You noticed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I said the witness could tell us whether it was a flat place, whether it was a meadow or not, but whether it's suitable for that, foundation would need to have been laid for that. Ms. Hochhauser then responded by asking one simple question, whether someone else said it's rocky, no, it's not rocky, it's a flat meadow. We leave it at that. I think I clearly indicated that also the Prosecution has to stay within the limits of what this witness can testify about. So therefore, don't use as an example the one and only where I immediately stopped the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Later, I will have to go back to individual incidents that you've testified about, but now I'd like to ask you something about the search for documents of the Army of Republika Srpska. You testified about that earlier on as well. Do you know how many requests you wrote altogether for receiving documentation of the Army of Republika Srpska, primarily the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: There must have been five or six over the years, I believe, formal, written requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that the replies from the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Republika Srpska and Serbia, were as follows: The archives are not accessible?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yeah, basically, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In 2006, all of a sudden, you received a message to the effect that archives were accessible and after that, you did get access to documents and you were told that these documents were collections of documents of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, of the Main Staff, as well as many other documents from other corps like the Drina Corps, the Herzegovina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These archives were in the basement of the Kozara barracks in Banja Luka when you arrived; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you also told that as part of the reforms in BH, in 2004, all military institutions were told that their documents should be sent to Banja Luka and that is how these documents reached the basement that you visited in 2006?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was the VRS documents that were to be sent to Banja Luka and the ABiH documents were to be sent to Sarajevo, but otherwise, your assertion is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. According to information received, the documentation of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps arrived there from a facility at Sokolac where it was allegedly found at the end of November or beginning of December 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was from Sokolac but I -- I'm not a hundred per cent sure whether it was at November/December 1994 but it was in that time period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you try to search these locations or facilities at Sokolac from where these archives had allegedly been transported so that you could see for yourself where they had been kept until then?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Microphone. You have to turn on your microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not -- I did not try to search that location after the archives were made available but I did try to search that location while we were still looking for the archives in the autumn of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The information that this documentation came from Sokolac, do you doubt that? Do you think it is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I have no reason to doubt that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to the documents of the Main Staff, whether these documents came from the same location, Sokolac, like the documents of the SRK, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The archivist might have told me, but I cannot recall at this moment, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, let us go back to how you searched this documentation that you were given access to in Banja Luka. You took an 11-member team there to Banja Luka in June and July 2006, an OTP team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have trained lawyers from the OTP on your team as well?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did any of the people you took along speak B/C/S fluently?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We had, I think, four or five language assistants and one of the attorneys from the OTP was fluent in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you speak or understand B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for processing these documents at the Kozara barracks in Banja Luka, am I right if I say that you and your team looked at the originals on the spot and then you chose the ones that you would scan and select and that you did all of that there and then?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: You are correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The archive of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps that you looked at contained tens of thousands of documents, and your team selected about 3 and a half thousand; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you something now about the archives of the Main Staff. Were there tens of thousands of these documents there as well, also accessible or available at that location?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many documents from the archive of the Main Staff were chosen or selected for scanning by your team?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't recall. I think it was in the neighbourhood of 2.000 documents, but I'd have to consult the spreadsheet to get an accurate number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in relation to the quantity of documents that you and your team selected, as compared to the entirety of the documents involved, of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, that is, do you agree that you selected five to 10 per cent of the overall number of documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it's obvious. 2.000 out of tens of thousands clearly is somewhere in that region. I mean, why ask this question? Doesn't assist in any way. It's a very small percentage. That's clear. I think the witness more or less testified to that when he said tens of thousands and most likely some 2.000 selected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But tens of thousands can be 2, 3, 4, 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, minimal percentage, very small percentage, whether it's 2, 3, 4, 5, doesn't change that in any way. Please provide -- please ask questions where the answers assist the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, would you agree with me that this selection of material was carried out according to a criterion that was primarily geared towards finding documents that you believed were of an accusatory nature, that is to say that would prove the guilt of the accused before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. We were equally diligent in looking for exculpatory material, and we specifically flagged and scanned any exculpatory material that we found.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now take a look at 1D1291 in e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, that is your testimony in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are going to need page 5 in e-court, and it should correspond to transcript page 11195.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From line 1, I'm going to quote. This is where the question starts. [In English] "And what criteria did you and others on the mission employ to decide what to copy and what not to copy?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were looking for, obviously, inculpatory documents because the purpose of the SRK research was to support the case against Dragomir Milosevic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please continue the quote, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My next question is dealing with the next part but I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It doesn't make really sense to split them up. Put your questions together in one and continue your quote. I will read. "We were also looking for exculpatory documents, which, for disclosure to the Defence team in this and other cases, and we were trying to get a comprehensive picture of the daily combat reports so we copied as many of those as we could locate." Please put your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did, and my question was, page 41, line 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, would you agree with me that this selection of material was carried out according to a criterion that was primarily geared towards finding documents that you believed were of an accuse nature; that is to say that would prove the guilt of the accused before this Tribunal? So the question was primarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a play of words, Mr. Lukic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, was your primary task to find inculpatory documents?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Question asked and answered, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot see where it was answered unless it's from what I read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Lukic. I'm not going to even further discuss the matter. The Prosecution, including its investigators, have an obligation to disclose any exculpatory documents they finds and if you ask me, Mr. Lukic, whether the primary purpose of an investigator is only to -- or to primarily focus on exculpatory documents, of course it's not. Of course, you work within the.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why does it bother you if I want to establish it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic I'm not in a debate. I'm telling you something. An investigator working for the Prosecution has a task to find all relevant documents related to the charges brought against or potential charges in the future. He, therefore, certainly will provide his employer with any inculpatory material and simultaneously he has an obligation to select any exculpatory documents which he finds so as to be disclosed to the Defence. The selection on what is and what is not relevant is a different matter. If there is any problem with that, but that's not about inculpatory or exculpatory. That can be dealt with apart and the Defence has all possibilities to challenge that primarily by saying that the selection is inadequate and does not deal with relevant materials and there are remedies for that, if needed, and the Chamber will always assist the Defence in finding those remedies and completing the body of evidence with such materials the Defence considers to be relevant. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just to indicate, the answer to your question is at page 41, lines 22 to 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is answer to exculpatory, and I was asking for inculpatory all the time. But I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you say -- if you're equally diligent for exculpatory documents, that means equally diligent in view of what is inculpatory material so therefore the question has been answered there. We are not here in a debating club. Would you please put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to go back to your dealing with sniping incidents and shelling incidents. Do you agree that the key point in your work was actually the contribution of witnesses or victims, that is to say to locate what happened where?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would agree that witnesses and victims are an extremely key point in the prosecution of any case, and I think it was a very important part of my role to locate them and to obtain statements which were to be supportive of their testimony. But there were many more tasks that I undertook which could also be classified as key points. To say that there was one key point, I just can't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you tell us, then, what the key point of your work was, in relation to sniping incidents and shelling incidents?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't -- I can't say that there was one key point. There were -- there was so much that contribute to an overall presentation of a case in court, gathering the evidence, locating the relevant investigation reports that were conducted by the local police at the time, or by UNPROFOR at the time, attending scenes, mapping.
