Basically gathering all the evidence that is presented in court. It's all key.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we see what you told us now, what your other duties were, and I'm going to ask you something in relation to that. Did you check the information that you received from witnesses through official documentation of the police or UNPROFOR in relation to these locations?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. We had access to the reports before we had access to the witnesses. It's my -- even though I wasn't involved in the selection of the various incidents when the indictment was first formulated, it's my understanding that a selection of the incidents was based on the documents from the local police and from the UNPROFOR, and then the witnesses were approached. So in that manner, yes, the information from the witnesses and the information from the reports were cross-checked and verified with one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say -- you say information was cross-checked. Did you cross-check information from police documents, from UNPROFOR documents, against the statements of witnesses who described when and where something happened?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. When you viewed a video about a certain incident in the Karadzic case, you noticed that the witness made a mistake and that it was not fair to ask that witness to identify the location. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I believe that was a shelling incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that witnesses, especially victims of trauma, may misremember facts related to the incident and misrepresent them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, whatever the witness says, the answer to the question for the Chamber is, yes, witnesses, victims of trauma, may misremember, just as everyone in life may misremember things from the past. It's a useless question. Let's get focused to what the evidence is. If there is any specific issue about a lack of recollection, let's go to that. Let's look at it. Let's take it seriously. But this kind of vague general questions within the general area of knowledge of everyone in this world do not assist the Chamber. But let's perhaps first take a break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and we resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue with the cross-examination, Mr. Lukic, could you give an answer to the question I put to the Defence before the break about the Prosecution's requests of yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I can, Your Honour. Our position is that the Prosecution had one year from February 2012 to February 2013, to arrange the expertise in question, and we received the expert report only in February 2013, and since that time we have been objecting. As far as the Defence is concerned, we have done nothing to be in the situation in which we are now where something needs to be rushed and urgently solved. We started objecting from February, from the moment you received the expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, there was a request for 65 ter meeting. Any special position on that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are always open for any kind of meetings only I cannot do that today, but somebody else maybe from the team can be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will consider your position and we'll see whether we can give a decision on the requests today. If not, it will be on Monday, but we will try to do our best to give it today due to the urgency of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, while thinking -- [Interpretation] While you are thinking about how to arrange the meeting, my colleague, Mr. Ivetic, just told me we are supposed to file eight submissions today. So this afternoon is really impossible for the Defence, as far as the meeting is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that additional submission. So you'd say on from 5.00, 4.00, then, after the filing is complete? No, no, I'm just kidding, Mr. Lukic. Apologies for that. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I also just ask the Chamber to refresh its memory to a discussion or something the Chamber said on the 22nd of August 2013 with respect to the length of the report, at T 15560 to -61. It was that statement made by the Chamber that led the Prosecution, perhaps incorrectly, but to believe that the issue had been resolved, and I can read it to the Chamber if that assists now. So Mr. Ivetic said: "If we could have one further clarification, Your Honours," and this is all relates to the Theunens report, "the 15th of February 2013, the Chamber indicated that 180 pages of the Theunens report needed to be revisited, whether they are necessary. Do we have a ruling, then, of the Chamber, are those included or excluded in the report so as to know what to respond to?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I do understand that the Prosecution takes the view that they are necessary. Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber said: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "And therefore still part of is, that how I have to --"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Mr. Ivetic."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Thank you, Your Honour." Judge Orie -- so then you -- Judge Orie gives the new filing date. So the Prosecution understood that the issue had been resolved --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- perhaps incorrectly now that the Chamber has made its decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't intend at that moment to say that the 180 pages were accepted, and I don't think I said that, as a matter of fact. I just tried to fully understand the position of the Prosecution, whether the Prosecution thought that the 180 pages were necessary, and I don't think I expressed anything as far as the position of the Chamber is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I accept that now, Your Honour. It's just the juxtaposition of Mr. Ivetic asking whether we had a ruling and then the Chamber made that statement. Again, I accept that perhaps that's misunderstood but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- so that the Chamber understands our surprise that the Chamber's decision was -- I thought that it had been resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand why you thought that. At the same time, I think certainly I have not been explicit in saying the Chamber accepts this or this is -- we'll also consider that and we'll see whether we can come to a conclusion later today or not. As soon as we have reached any conclusion, then we will immediately inform the parties about it. Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, one of the -- I think it was yesterday that we had an issue with adding a page to a document which was already, I would say, locked by the -- locked by the registrar. Let me just find my notes on the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll find them in a minute. Mr. Lukic, you may proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, just one question: Am I supposed to understand your testimony today as saying that you used police and UNPROFOR files and cross checked them with witness statements at the moment when the witnesses were pointing the locations of the incidents to you?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. This -- when I was referring to cross checking, that was in preparation of the whole case. When we did the filming and the 360 panoramas, we did not rehearse the witnesses or victims at all. They were not permitted to review their statements, they were not permitted to look at the photographs or look at police reports, they came into it and just told us as the best of -- and showed us, rather, the best of their recollection at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Earlier today on page 46, and this confused me, line 5, I'll read out what I asked you and what you answered. [In English] "Q. You say, you say information was cross checked. Did you cross check information from police documents, from UNPROFOR documents, against the statements of witnesses who described when and where something happened?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes."

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but you must realise that when we did this filming and the 360, it was not the first time I had ever met these witnesses. I had met these witnesses many times before. I had taken statements from these witnesses before we did the filming.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just tell us, in conclusion, when you filmed, is the only source what the witnesses showed you or you compared it with what they had said earlier at the moment when you are filming? Did you check what they said earlier to you, to the police, to the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was aware of what they had said earlier but I did not -- I did not correct the witnesses when we were filming. That was not the purpose of the filming. If they made mistakes, so be it. Their filming was to assist the parties during the witness's testimony in court, and their testimony could be tested by cross-examination in the various trials. So if they showed me a location that was where we filmed it. If they showed me a way that they were standing, that was how we filmed it. If they showed me a direction from which a shot came, that was how we filmed it. I did not correct them and I did not confront them at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These GPS readings that you also recorded and testified to, would it be correct to say that these readings were made on the basis of where the victims were standing or where the witness said the victim was standing, not on the basis of official documents?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Where the victims or the witnesses indicated that they had been standing or positioned at the time. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You used the Garmin E Track GPS device. Is it correct that you are not in a position to give us the technical specification and the margin of error of this device?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were two margins of error. First of all, the technical specifications, no, I'm afraid not. The margin of error -- there are two margins of error. One is -- at that time was inherently built into a GPS unit. Nowadays, of course, GPS units are much more sophisticated and accurate within metres. Examples are the instruments that are within vehicles to give you direction through streets of towns. The second margin of error is based on the number of satellites that are accessed by the instrument in order to obtain a reading. The minimum number is three satellites to give a triangulation of your location or height. The more satellites you can access, the more accurate the reading is. And with three satellites, I think the margin of error was, like, 35 metres or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more technical matter. You will know this. For the purpose of gathering GPS information, did you use the geographic -- universal geographic coordinate system or the transversal coordinate system or some other system?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: When I was filming with the witnesses, I had the GPS unit set on -- to display degrees, minutes and seconds. It can be switched by pressing a few buttons into displaying the coordinates in UTM, universal transversal mercator, or by switching another setting to decimal degrees. So when I first recorded it, I saved them in degrees, minutes, seconds. However, when I returned from that mission to The Hague and consulted my colleagues in the mapping unit to start plotting those locations, turned out that his software was suitable to accept degrees, decimals. So I don't recall if we had to access another computer programme to switch them or if I had -- still had the GPS unit and I could just change the settings to get the decimal degrees. One way or the other, though, we converted them into decimal degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also the case that these readings generated by the GPS device, you did not try to compare them with the existing UNPROFOR maps that were available for any of the incidents in question?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. I don't think I compared them with an UNPROFOR map. The purpose of these GPS readings was just to put the dots on the map for the benefit of the parties during the trial so that they could orient themselves within the city. And obviously, the dots themselves probably measure by a hundred metres or 150 metres in diameter. So the GPS readings are simply to put those dots there, to orient the parties. They are not to make a comparison with UNPROFOR maps and try to clarify any previous investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I had some other questions related to that, but you have just obviated the need for them because they all go below 100, 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the GPS is not the main guiding thing. It is, as I do understand you well, it is an instrument that can assist for further action to be taken. What we have, of course, as the primary source of what happened, is the videos. And where the witness said they stood. Therefore, that's at least how the Chamber understands the GPS readings in the context of the investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I will not ask my additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you maybe pay attention to the number of satellites from which you were receiving signals, because of this margin of error?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would have seen it on the screen of the unit, but I did not make a note of it, I didn't record it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So these measurements were not meant to replace the witness statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If somebody said during cross-examination here something different to these measurements, we should accept that testimony rather than the measurement made by you and your team?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I object to that question. It's broad and unclear, if somebody -- if there was something said during cross-examination that he wants to put to this witness that's one thing but as a general statement I just don't think that's a fair question to ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whether we should accept the testimony rather than the measurement, that's of course for the Chamber to decide. We have to balance all the evidence and make our findings, and what then is to rely upon is for the Chamber to decide, not for a witness to testify about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honours, if I may say this. The purpose of this question was that most of these witnesses did not come to testify, so we wanted to see what about their statements, what to do with these measurements that are related to the statements of witnesses who have not testified. Of course, it's up to you to decide. I just wanted to explain my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is any inconsistency between testimony or statements, or -- and the GPS readings, take us to them and we'll have a look at it. That's the most important thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I should like to ask you something about the features located close to the measurement sites. While taking measurements, did you make note and did you pay attention to the features and installations that existed during the war and that belonged to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, as you said speaking to the witnesses and taking these measurements, that victims and witnesses are, in fact, not in a position to establish from which location a bullet or a shell arrived from injuring people? So not the direction but the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the basis of?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: On the basis, again, that he's asking this witness to supplant what the Chamber's evaluation is, it's up to the Chamber to decide whether a witness was able to appropriately identify where a shot came from. Based on all of the evidence in front of it. It's not for this witness to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, of course, first and foremost, we should look at whether this witness drew any conclusions on the basis of any such an observation by a witness. Did you ever rely on a witness telling you what the source of fire, I'm not asking about the direction but the source of fire was, during an interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if there are any further questions in this context, please put them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's it, Your Honour, that's what I wanted. Thank you. If I may consult with my colleague for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Among the incidents you investigated, did you investigate a shelling that happened on the 28th of May, 1992, from Sirokaca, G1?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Near Sirokaca, G1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have taken some statements regarding 28th of May, 1992, but I don't recall actually doing a physical investigation of any shelling sites.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interject but just to be clear G1 refers to a mass bombardment of the entire city, so if there is a specific impact that counsel is asking about I'm requesting that he be a little more specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we do have a concrete incident but I don't know, I'm just a bit confused with the answer that the gentleman did not took part in any investigation of a bombing incidents, [Overlapping speakers] incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not -- he was talking about physical investigation. That is not the same as an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I will ask this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall talking to Fadila Tarcin regarding this incident? She testified to the incident referred to here as G1.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The name is familiar but I don't recall if I took -- I did an interview with her or my colleague did an interview with her, but it's very, very possible that I interviewed her and took a statement in regards to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since Mrs. Tarcin, on the transcript page 3447 to 3448, testifying before this Trial Chamber, confirmed that the damage to the neighbour's house from the shell that injured her was facing the city of Sarajevo; that is to say, the territory controlled by the BH Army. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I -- I'm not familiar with the testimony of Mrs. Tarcin. I didn't read any transcripts, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I only asked if you knew. If you don't, it's all right. I will now ask you something about this investigation carried out by Colonel Demurenko, and we will refer specifically to way-points. Can you tell us what exactly was the task entrusted to you regarding Colonel Demurenko's video? What task was given to you by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The original idea was to go to the locations which he had identified in his video and to obtain photographs of those locations, to see whether, indeed, they were physically unsuitable for mortar locations, mortar sites. Now, obviously I only went to two spots on that -- that he had indicated, at the 3.400 metre mark and the 3.600 metre mark, because the other locations within the VRS lines at 2.000 metres and 2.700 metres, were in places which did not have a hard surface road leading to them. And when I arrived in Sarajevo before proceeding to Mount Trebevic, I consulted the mine action centre to see what the risk of mines and unexploded ordnance would be in that area and there had been a great deal of clearance in the area, immediately around those two spots, but they could not guarantee that they had recovered every piece of unexploded ordnance. Therefore, I didn't deem it safe for myself and my interpreter to go to those last two locations at 2.000 metres and 2.700 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that before you set out, you asked the mapping unit of the OTP to draw for you a map of the location that Colonel Demurenko identified?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. And that's the exhibit that was referred to earlier, the satellite photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have seen lines drawn, and on those lines is it the case that you did not tour the territory that was controlled during the war by the BH Army, only the territory controlled by the VRS, by the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: On this particular mission, I did not go to each location on the ABiH side simply because Colonel Demurenko did not do so. I have been to those locations during the course of my other duties in Sarajevo, but not for this particular exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you visited these locations, were you alone or did you take with you somebody who had military training such as an artillery or a mortar officer?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just for my clarification, is it no, I was not alone, no, I did not go with somebody with knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry for not being clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question is compound, it's not your problem. It's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was -- I was with a language assistant, with no other persons, so -- had no military training or artillery or mortar officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read something out from the Karadzic transcript of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpreted] 1D1291. Could we please have that in e-court now? I think that in this way we are going to cut things shorter. We should have transcript page 111226 from the Karadzic transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read lines 11 through 25. [In English] I quote. Answer -- and it's your answer, sir. I quote: "During his testimony, the Defence case for Dragomir Milosevic, Colonel Demurenko produced a -- or showed a video and testified that the investigation conducted by both UNPROFOR and the local Bosnian investigators revealed the angle at which the 120-millimetre mortar impacted the street in front of the market building, and the direction of fire of that mortar. Using a mortar table for an M52 mortar, Colonel Demurenko, in the video and in his testimony, worked out the six possible points at which that mortar would have been fired. He testified, and he stated on the -- in the video that he physically attended, along with VRS soldiers, the three possible sites on the VRS side of the confrontation lines and viewed the ground within a ten metre radius of those sites and found no signs of a mortar having been fired. Therefore, he said that if it did not come from those three particular sites within ten metre radius, it could not have originated from the VRS side." [Interpretation] Sir, does this excerpt from the transcript precisely record your response with regard to this subject?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The answer is truthful and today you would give the same answer to that question; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was truthful, but I believe I left out the part from his video where he said that the ground was rocky and steep and unsuitable to put on -- a mortar in. In his testimony I think he said he had seen no signs of a mortar having been fired. In the video he said that it was rocky and steep.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, was it your understanding that Colonel Demurenko had just found that there were no traces of mortar activity, or did his examinations of the possible firing points include other checks, in terms of ruling those places out as locations from which shells were fired that hit Markale?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "include other checks." I'm not sure what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, for instance, did he say where the mortar would have to be positioned, from the wall, from the forest? Would you remember that? Actually we are going to take a look at a video now and I'm going to ask my colleague, Mr. Ivetic, to play 1D607 for us, from 7 minutes 38 seconds to 9 minutes 49 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Lukic, may I add to your quote the question that was asked, whether the witness could briefly describe the view or theory as he understood it. Now, I do understand that this witness has not specifically formed an opinion about the value of that, but he just checked whether, at the places indicated, whether he found rocky situation and that he now tells us that he found meadows or flat places or solid places, and whenever he started telling us whether these are suitable locations for mortar fire, I stopped the witness because there is no foundation for that. Let's keep this in mind if you put your questions -- your following questions to the witness after we have viewed the video. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we play the video now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no sound at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The sound quality was a bit poor, but I imagine that you listened to this a countless number of times in order to go on this mission in the first place so I assume that you do know what it is that Colonel Demurenko is talking about.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, obviously I haven't memorised it but I do -- have listened to it before, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see that Colonel Demurenko is mentioning some photographs. Did you ever have an opportunity of seeing the photographs mentioned by Colonel Demurenko and did you compare them to the locations that you visited in order to establish whether these were the same locations?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I did see the photographs and some of them are just in the middle of trees. There is one photograph of a meadow. However, it's not the same meadow that I visited.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this part of the video, it seems that the Colonel is indicating that the terrain and the forest are on the Serb side, which also makes it inconvenient for firing mortar shells. Do you know how far away a mortar has to be from a forest or from a tree? Did you bear that in mind when you examined certain locations?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going to be that question, Judge. I think the -- Mr. Lukic already asked in the beginning about this witness's experience with artillery and mortars, and in light of the Court's guidance about what areas he's able to testify about, I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This witness has no drawn any conclusions as to -- as to whether mortars could be fired from those locations. Apart from that, Mr. Lukic, it's relatively easy. If you have the angle and if you know approximately how large the trees are, it's not that difficult to -- even for lay persons, but this witness came as a witness of fact, but looking at the photographs of the meadows, and if a mortar is fired at 40 or 50 or 60 degrees, I even could give a fairly clear estimate on the basis of those photographs whether they would pass the trees "yes" or "no," but of course, I will not do that. I would seek evidence to rely upon for that and those trees in the pictures would be part of that evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you carry out any examinations in terms of vegetation or the terrain that you visited in order to establish whether there had been any changes that had taken place either in a natural way or in an artificial way, in order to affect the terrain or vegetation in the area?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you now explain to us how you saw yourself at that moment? I think that the answer is going to be negative, but I have to ask you this: Did you consider yourself at any point in time, when you were given this mission, to investigate Colonel Demurenko's findings, did you understand your mission to be that of an expert who was supposed to be refute Colonel Demurenko's findings?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not an expert. Just an investigator to verify his findings. And obviously did not verify his findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would just like to ask you briefly, you mentioned Mr. van der Weijden today as well so I would like us to take a look at an incident from his report. It is a document under seal. P1130. It is a document that is also associated with your testimony. First of all, I would like to ask you whether you participated in Mr. van der widen's work on this report?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not participate in his report. The -- I was limited to taking him to the various locations in Sarajevo. The way he wrote his report was his own input.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 13 of this report and further on in English, and page 16 and further on in B/C/S. It is incident F1. If we look at the third paragraph on page 13 in e-court, in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. van der Weijden identifies Baba Stijena, Spicasta Stijena, 920 metres away from the location where the incident took place to the alleged location where the shooter was. Was that also your finding on the basis of GPS measurements?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first question should be whether the witness made any finding in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You're asking me about the distance, the 920 metres?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the first question was whether you made any findings as was part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall taking GPS readings from the location where the victim was, but I don't recall taking a GPS reading from the -- from the Baba Stijena. So I may have done so. I just don't recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Lukic, you are making Baba Stijena and Spicasta Stijena the same. As far as I remember these are totally different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My mistake, it's Baba Stijena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's Baba Stijena, yes. Now did you make any finding between where the witness was and where you photographed and a location called Baba Stijena? Did you measure the distance between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I may have, Your Honour. I just don't recall. But in regards to that distance, I was standing beside Mr. van der Weijden when he used a laser range finder so I would -- no matter what -- I would not dispute his distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say you witnessed that he apparently was busy measuring a distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll go back to Baba Stijena. We will discuss that. But now I would like us to move on to your testimony with regard to Mr. Demurenko. Let's go back to that. Although I did ask you why you went only to Serb territory, did you know that it was stated in the UNPROFOR report that it's possible that the projectile was fired from a distance between 1.500 to 3.500 metres?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask during these technical kinds of questions that we be directed to the UNPROFOR report in question, by 65 ter or exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're invited to give the source for what you asked the witness, whether he has any knowledge about. But if he doesn't know it, then you don't even have to look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I can show P797.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's first see whether the witness can -- we can look at it closer if the witness says that he is aware of that. Did you know that UNPROFOR would have stated that the -- that it's possible that the projectile was fired from a distance between 1500 and 3.500 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's -- I don't recall that in the UNPROFOR report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, we don't have to further pursue this matter but, of course, the issue is whether it's possible, yes, of course, then the next question is is that the only possibility or are there more possibilities? That's -- we would have to look at that document but the witness can't tell us anything about it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a technical question. I have an entire series of questions, but you can tell us if you cannot answer. Do you know what the longest distance is from which a 120-millimetre shell could have been fired from and for it to be able to fall in front of the market?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The only information I have in that regard is what Colonel Demurenko demonstrated on the video. According to his calculations the farthest distance was 3.600 metres. I don't know the actual technical capabilities of a 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep matters short. If you don't know, then -- Mr. Lukic, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will leave this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it correct that you investigated the area that is delineated by an azimuth of 160 and 170 degrees?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was it that you investigated, which range, then?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I concentrated on 176 degrees. There is also a line drawn on the satellite image of 170 degrees. And I stopped at other way-points but they were not within the 170 or 176 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now take a look at this document? Just a moment, please. Let me find the number. P380. P2380, I'm sorry. Mr. Hogan, we see here some points that were marked WP. However, these are letters. Are you able to mark the points that these letters refer to? Because I did not manage to see that in this photograph. Can you mark the points for us now, the ones that you visited?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, actually, there is a small black crescent beside each WP number. I realise it's difficult to see on the e-court, but the mid-point of that crescent is the point. That's the point. I can mark them if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Oh, I can see now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can see them all, it's the crescents being part of a circle and the centre of that circle would be -- is that how we have to understand it or is it the centre of linking the two extremities of the -- what we find there, the crescent.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's on the arc of the partial circle. So the centre of that arc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The centre of the arc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we zoom in on the lower part of the picture then we can see it more clearly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I'm past the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're looking at the clock. You're not the only one. We will take a break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you give us an indication as to how much more time you would need? We gained the impression that you had to skip under the guidance of the Chamber quite a few matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe after the break, I can give you a better estimation but I will go through incidents, and it's really focused on what this gentleman did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on what he did. Not on the incident itself, which he did not investigate. Let's try to keep that very clear on our minds. We might need a bit of time, dependent on what happens during the break, to deal with some of the other procedural matters as well. We take a break and we will resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to briefly deal with a few procedural matters. I think it was yesterday that we had an issue with adding a page to a document which was already in the hands of the Registry, was already MFI'd or admitted into evidence. It's only the Registry who can make changes to e-court in relation to such documents and such documents will not be unlocked by the Registry for the parties to execute any changes and to the extent there may have been any misunderstanding. That's the system. And the parties are invited if anything has to be added, either to provide the addition, which would then be attached to the document in e-court or to upload the then-complete version which may then replace the original one. If there is any problem there, don't hesitate to ask Madam Registrar about it. Then I would also deal with the matter we earlier discussed this morning and which was raised by the Defence yesterday. The Chamber has -- the Prosecution has made yesterday a number of requests in relation to the upcoming testimony of expert witness Theunens and the Chamber now delivers its decision on these requests. The Chamber has considered the submissions of the parties in this request. The Chamber has also reviewed the relevant transcript pages and finds that both in view of the stage of the proceedings at that moment in relation to this -- to the expert report and on the basis of the wording found in those transcripts, that the Chamber did not express itself in any way on finally accepting or not accepting the position of the Prosecution. Now, as for the request for the Chamber to reconsider its decision concerning part 1 of the Theunens report, the Chamber reminds the Prosecution that no decision on admission has been taken and the Prosecution's request is therefore moot because there is no decision which is there to be reconsidered. The Chamber has only announced that it is inclined to deny the admission of part 1 of the report and it is asking the Prosecution to adjust the examination of Theunens accordingly and has done that a couple of days in advance of the start of his testimony. The Chamber considered that making this announcement prior to the testimony was a transparent and correct way to proceed. The Chamber is ready to listen to any proposal the Prosecution has on how to best elicit the most relevant information dealt with in part 1, short of having the whole part admitted into evidence. For example, the Prosecution could consider tendering a drastically reduced selection of part 1, perhaps in the area of 10 or 15 per cent of it, which, together with the focused examination of Theunens, could provide the Chamber with the information needed. In this respect, the Prosecution should also take into account what is already in evidence concerning the material covered by part 1 so as to avoid repetitious evidence. With regard to the request to hold a 65 ter meeting, the Chamber strongly urges the parties to meet to discuss where the area of dispute are in order to achieve a focused examination of the witness. The Chamber is, however, not inclined to hold a 65 ter meeting for that purpose. Finally, the Prosecution requests an opportunity, after the completion of the testimony of Theunens, to assess which of his conclusions have been challenged during cross-examination and which documents therefore need to be tendered. The Chamber would like this assessment to be done while the witness is testifying. The Chamber would be ready to grant a reasonable amount of time between cross-examination and re-examination during which the Prosecution could consider which documents it needs to tender in light of the cross-examination. The tendering of these documents should then be done during the re-examination of Theunens. And this concludes the Chamber's decision on the matter. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. I see Mr. Groome, you are still reading from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm still trying to absorb everything that the Chamber has said. If the Prosecution were to proceed with Mr. Theunens in the way suggested here by the Chamber, then when the Chamber finally entered its decision about how much of part 1 would be introduced, would the Prosecution have an opportunity to recall him for -- to deal with the parts of the report that the Chamber declined to admit provided the Prosecution was able to persuade the Chamber that they were relevant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We would seriously consider that, upon an application made. I don't give any guarantees in advance, as you'll understand. I see the problem for the Prosecution, what you leave out, and is finally lost is perhaps you consider that to be a risk. We will seriously consider any such thing upon an application.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and you asked about my estimate. I went through the questions and they are more focused actually on the real work of Mr. Hogan so -- but I'll still need at least three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider in view of what you have done and what you are now about to do, whether the Chamber will grant so much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And another submission should probably be made, be done by the Prosecution. They want to have their next protected witness on Monday first.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, as you can see Mr. Groome just stepped out but that was the information that I had from him that if we can continue with that witness on Monday and interrupt Mr. Hogan's testimony for that purpose, because I think that witness is scheduled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, before the Chamber also starts deciding on how you would use your time on the suggestions of the parties, would you be available a little bit more next week if we would not continue on Monday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's appreciated. Mr. Lukic, then we'll again listen to you carefully. There were some problems in relation to staying within the limits of what the witness could tell us. We'll see how it develops, your cross-examination develops, over the next half an hour. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, on this photograph before us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could zoom in on the last two-thirds of the picture, the bottom two-thirds, this is approximately what we saw when Judge Fluegge asked for this view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I first ask one very factual question? The distances measured on this projection are those distances which include the difference in altitude or are they just the projection on a map of the distances? You understand the difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour, and the answer is that it's the distance projected on the map, does not take into account the difference in altitude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what we say 2.000 metres could be, if measured with your, what is it your laser machine, could be quite different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because laser machine, as I understand, gives a -- measures directly from the point where the machine is used in a direct line to the position where the object is to which you measure the distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and that's what this is meant to depict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So if there was a line of sight between each location and the market, that would be that distance, and the line of sight does not take into account walking distance up and down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about something different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you take triangle, if you have a point which is at the basis of the triangle and if at the top of the triangle there is the other point you want to measure the distance to, that is, I think it's called the hypotenuse but I'm not quite sure whether I remember well from secondary school.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hypotenuse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, that's -- we learned it in Greek or in Latin, then you have the direct distance between one point and the other. Another way is to project it as you see it on a map, which does not take into consideration any difference in altitude, and then you would just measure the basis of the triangle to the point where -- the point you want to measure projects under an angle of 90 degrees to the basis of that triangle. Am I clear enough?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is what I was referring to and not to any up and down walking the distance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour. And the answer is that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know. And do you know, having looked at what Mr. Demurenko presented, what he used for distances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That does not make the matter any less complex than it was already. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not receive English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Courtesy of the officers of the Tribunal we received now a zoomed in view of the last bottom two-thirds, is it all right now? On this photograph, now that you have explained what these crescents mean, we see which points you had in mind when you were doing this verification. My earlier question was: Is it the case that you checked between angles 160 and 176 and you said no, I checked between 180 and 176. On this photograph, we see that the crescents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we check that on the transcript, whether that's what the witness said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't remember 180 to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, it's 170.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did mention 80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we find in the transcript where the witness said that? Let me be --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 180 only appears in relation to the number of pages of the Theunens report, on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I should start my question from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please and give a detailed reference to the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the page 67, line 5, my question was: "Is it correct that you investigated the area that is delineated by the azimuth of 160 and 170 degrees? "A. No." "What was it that you investigated, which range, then? "I concentrated on 176 degrees. There is also a line drawn on the satellite image of 170 degrees and I stopped at other way-points but they were not within the 170 or 176 degrees."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So my question is: These way-points, WP 5, 10 and 6, are, in fact, outside the range between 170 and 176, and they lean towards 160?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is yes to this question, Mr. Lukic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did you investigate the area outside the range between 170 and 176 degrees?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: My task was initially, or my purpose initially, was to go to the four way-points along the 176 degree mark, to test the veracity of Colonel Demurenko's assertions that he had made on the video. Since I could only get to the two, I was not able to get to the two way-points that were closest to the city, I had extra time and when I had passed the location that's marked as way-point 5, to get to the way-point 2 and 3, it struck me as being quite an attractive spot for any -- in any case, it was flat, it was level, it was -- had tracks leading off in different directions. And when I was at way-point 2, I looked up on the ridge and there appeared to be, towards the east, there appeared to be a road up there somewhere, so I determined to myself to try to find that and that led me to way-point 10 and way-point 6 where I also took some photographs because they were nice and flat and firm ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, you earlier explained to us that you were equally focused on all relevant information, whether inculpatory or exculpatory. Have you also photographed all those places which you considered not to be flat, to be rocky, et cetera, so as to give a balanced impression of the whole of the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is certainly some of that visible in many of the photographs, Your Honour, that I took, over a hundred photographs. Steep slopes in the distance, heavily wooded areas, rocky ground, but I did not stop at each and every location and take photographs, close-ups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because beyond what your primary task was, you selected places from where you thought it might be suitable places for firing, and you did not focus on places which you thought not useful places for firing. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's accurate, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this map, we see WP 6. Why did you measure this way-point, which is obviously four kilometres away? Why did you photograph and note a point which is almost four kilometres away from the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was just because I had reached the end of that road and I made -- had to turn around and go back the way I came and I think I just took a way-point measurement and took some photographs from that location. I don't recall any other specific purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How familiar are you with the findings and conclusions of either the Bosnian police or UNPROFOR as to the type of charges that could have been used for the shell that exploded at Markale market? And do you know which charge should have been used, must have been used, from way-points 10, 6 and 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I object to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the witness has any knowledge about it, but from what we heard until now, and where he has said he has no expert knowledge of mortars, then I would be surprised if he would be able to tell us. But if you, for any reason, can tell us, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm afraid I can't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The reason for my question was to find out on what this investigation concentrated, as far as the evidence of Mr. Demurenko is concerned. If that is your answer, I'll accept it. We have measured this point, WP 6, and we found that it is exactly 3.933 metres away from the point of impact and the azimuth is 166.4. Is that what you recorded as WP 6?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, how did you measure your 3.933 metres? There are two systems, as I indicated before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the same way Mr. Hogan measured, with the laser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With a laser. I would be surprised that with the mountains in between you could a use a laser for that. Apart from that, I learned from Mr. Hogan that this measurement was measured on the basis of a projection in a flat area. So I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I might be wrong, I might be wrong because here I have both versions noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two questions if you're wrong. Are you wrong in what Mr. Hogan told us how he measured or are you wrong in the way you say you measured it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the way I said we measured it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You measured it also on the projection on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It adds to the complexity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not my intention. I'm sorry. But can I ask Mr. Hogan still if he can confirm that is -- that it actually corroborates his findings, is it approximate or exact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The degrees and the -- I have never measured it myself but I do not dispute your measurements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the altitude of this point is 1.198 metres? It's in your table, in fact.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this map the way we zoomed in now, or perhaps it's better to see the entire photograph, which is now on the screen, can you say for the purposes of this case, as you did in the Karadzic case, can you mark the separation line between the two warring parties?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on the central part of the image, it would be helpful. Thank you. The separation line ran along -- or the -- the forward front lines of the VRS ran along the Pale road at this location. So they would have run like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May I tender this as a Defence Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number D374, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D374 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I, at this point, put one question to the witness. How did you select these way-points as depicted here in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean from 2 till 10, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The way-point 2 and 3 were selected on the basis of Colonel Demurenko's video, so my whole purpose was to go to there, to those two points, plus the 2700 metre point and the 2.000 metre point along the azimuth of 176 degrees. While I was in the area on Trebevic because so many of the trial team had not been up there in the past, I also stopped at these other places at random, at wide spaces on the road, flat spaces on the road, and just took a measurement and photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now call up in e-court 65 ter 19792, Prosecution number. We need page 48 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph that you took; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the background we see Mount Igman and Mount Bjelasnica; correct?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not certain. It could be, but I can't orient myself as to the direction I'm facing in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we, alongside this photograph, that is to say on a split screen, display 1D1296, also a photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a photo taken by the Defence team, and we believe we did so from the same place where you took yours. We only turned the lens more towards the city. Do you know that OP 4, the observation post 4 of the UNPROFOR, would certainly have registered firing from this location? Do you know where OP 4 was?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: OP 4? No, I'm not -- I can't remember where OP 4. OP 1, but I'm not sure exactly where OP 4 was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, if I look at these photographs, I have great difficulties in accepting that it was taken from the same place because on the left photograph taken by the Defence I see a lot of what appear to be high-rise buildings, whereas on the right photograph, I don't see any of that. On the right photograph, I see a totally different structure of mountainous area at the back, which seems not to appear on the left-hand area. It may be taken from the same point but then certainly in a different direction, and I do not know what direction. Therefore, to start hearing evidence on the basis of this, we would need to know more. Mr. Lukic, is there any way where the photographs, for example, overlap?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that I mentioned that the lens of the camera was moved to another direction from the same spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then of course what you usually would expect is that you take at least a part of the photograph where there is some overlap so that we can follow exactly how it develops.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will do that -- I don't have it with me now, Your Honour, but probably will have to do this exercise again. What we wanted to show is that OP 4 is exactly below this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: OP 4 is below any point which is higher up, I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But in the direction, in between Markale 2, Markale 2 incident and this spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we know exactly from where this photograph was taken, the photograph taken by Mr. Hogan? We know exactly where it was taken. If we know where OP 4 is then we don't need this trees and, et cetera, in order to find out where it is in relation to the other thing. That's -- it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan said that he does not know where OP 4 is so I have to leave this area of my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that I was allowed to check it with Mr. Hogan. Now I know that he does not know but I didn't know that before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you could have asked him do you know where OP 4 is without any photographs. He would have said no and we would have moved on. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I had to connect it with photographs. Okay. Anyways, thank you. Can we see 65 ter 19792, please? And I need -- we can have it only that on the screen. We need page 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The place that you marked as WP 6 is next to a narrow road covered with rocks and rather steep. This photograph shows a part of this area; right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So since the Prosecution didn't offer this page into evidence, we would kindly ask to have this page as next Defence exhibit. Or the whole exhibit would be offered. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I was actually going to suggest at this point based on the number of questions from everybody, I think that the whole exhibit, not just the selection that the Prosecution had tendered, be offered. We had tried to select a small amount but I think at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All hundred?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that the parties sit together and agree on what they consider to be relevant before we start looking at a hundred photographs instead of 10 or 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties are invited to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In any case I don't have an objection to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we then ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not in a hurry with that so -- I know that you have some deadlines, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, yeah. So it's -- I think the end of our working day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not of the working day, but at least of the -- today's court hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The trial day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hogan, I again would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony or to communicate in any other way about your testimony with -- irrespective whom. We would like to see you back but not on Monday morning. If you would be kind enough to follow the guidance that you will receive through the victims and witness section and then be with us again once we can continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: As the witness is leaving the courtroom can I just quickly take this opportunity say that the revised version of P2382 is -- has been uploaded as instructed under document ID 0619-7138-1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When it comes to numbers, I do not know exactly what they stand for very often. This is in the series of the -- of the material provided --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, yeah, I apologise. It was if you recall I had failed have the index uploaded and now this is the corrected exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And it has been -- yes, Madam Registrar, therefore can either attach -- have you uploaded only that one page or have you --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I believe the entire -- we have re-uploaded the entire exhibit as instructed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, leave is granted to replace the existing version of P2382 by the newly uploaded ID as appears in the transcript. Are there any other matters? Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I discussed what the Chamber said earlier about Mr. Theunens with the team. The Prosecution would be prepared to go forward with his evidence next week. It would of course take additional time, the Chamber didn't rule on the application for additional time in excess of the 200 hours. Once I had the Registry reports this week I will see what available time we have left and we will be expanding that examination. By the looks of things now, it seems that he would not be testifying until Wednesday morning. That's what my calculation of the projection of the schedule. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
